sections.text: The US government has suspended Microsoft and seven other technology firms, including Adobe, from a program that helps foreign workers obtain permanent US residency. The Department of Labor announced it will not process new or pending applications from these firms.

sections.text: Vance claimed Microsoft laid off American workers while filing thousands of visa applications, undercutting domestic wages. Microsoft rejected these allegations, stating that eighty per cent of its H-1B filings were for existing employees rather than new hires, and that its international staff receive the same compensation as US workers. sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: In September 2022, underwater explosions ruptured the Nord Stream pipelines beneath the Baltic Sea. Following an investigation, German police traced evidence to Ukraine and arrested former Special Forces soldier Serhii K in Italy. Prosecutors allege he led deep-sea divers on a rented yacht to plant explosives. Both Serhii K and Ukraine deny involvement.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The blasts severed Russian gas deliveries to Germany, raising questions over attacks on civilian infrastructure. The trial causes diplomatic unease between Berlin and Kyiv. In Germany, the far-right AfD party has used the case to oppose further military aid to Ukraine, whilst some Ukrainians view the pipelines as legitimate Russian war assets.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Next week, Serhii K will go on trial in Hamburg charged with causing an explosion and a war crime. His defence will argue he cannot disclose military activities. Meanwhile, a second suspect, Volodymyr Zhuravlyov, is contesting extradition to Germany from Croatia.

gist: An infected Kenyan businessman travelled across three countries before dying from Ebola in Nairobi.
His infection went undetected through several medical facilities and two airport health screenings.
Dozens of potential contacts have been quarantined as health authorities trace his movements.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: A Kenyan businessman fell ill in DR Congo, visited several medical facilities, and crossed into Uganda. He then flew to Nairobi via Entebbe, passing airport temperature screenings undetected. Diagnosed with Ebola after arriving at Nairobi Hospital, he died on 5 October.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The incident exposed weaknesses in regional biosecurity and airport screening during an outbreak that has killed over 4,000 people in DR Congo. Experts warned that relying solely on temperature checks is limited, as medications or absence of fever can mask symptoms.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Kenyan authorities have quarantined potential contacts, while tracing continues across DR Congo and Uganda. The WHO is working to counter fear and misinformation, warning that stigma discourages people from reporting symptoms and seeking timely care.
